title: Stop a rolled back order sending its confirmation mail
summary: An @EventListener sent mail in the middle of the transaction, so it moves to @TransactionalEventListener, and logging the mail walks into the propagation trap.

turns.user: got a complaint that someone got a confirmation mail for an order that rolled back (out of stock). how

assistant.body: An @EventListener runs synchronously, right where publishEvent is called. The mail goes out inside place, and when stock.reserve throws afterwards and the order rolls back, the mail has already been sent. A @TransactionalEventListener holds the event until the transaction finishes. With phase AFTER_COMMIT it only runs once the commit succeeds, and never after a rollback. This guarantees a rolled back order never gets a mail. Note: the reverse holds too. If sending fails, the order is already committed and stays that way.

turns.user: fixed. while youre there, log each sent mail to mail_log. audit wants it

assistant.body: Sure! The listener takes a MailLogRepository and saves a row after sending. The row should live in the same transaction as the order, so @Transactional states Propagation.REQUIRED explicitly. Now the order and its mail record are written together.

turns.user:
now it doesnt start
IllegalStateException: @TransactionalEventListener method must not be annotated with @Transactional unless when declared as REQUIRES_NEW or NOT_SUPPORTED

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was wrong. By the time an AFTER_COMMIT listener runs, the order's transaction has already committed. The connection is still bound to the thread, though, so REQUIRED joins that finished transaction. The save goes through without an error, no commit ever follows, and mail_log stays empty. In other words, a write that vanishes silently. Since Spring 6.1 that combination is rejected at startup, which is the check you hit. REQUIRES_NEW opens a transaction of its own.
